newsitem.title: REPUBLIC OF IRELAND: Irish bonds firm on back of rampant German bunds.
newsitem.headline: Irish bonds firm on back of rampant German bunds.

text.p: Irish bonds firmed in busy late trade on Friday, mostly on the back of rampant German bunds which also dragged UK gilts and U.S. Treasuries higher, dealers said.
Dealers said bunds had risen on a short covering rally.

"The markets are very strong really. German bunds are having a great day and are up about three-quarters of a point on the back of good sentiment. Irish bonds are not up quite as much but have been pulled higher," one dealer said.
"You'd think there might be fears of a correction, the market has gone so high. But that has not been the case," the dealer added.

By 1605 GMT, the 6.5 percent bond due 2001 had gained 30 pence from Thursday's close to 102.75 to yield 5.75 percent while the eight percent bond due 2006 had risen 45 pence to 110.25 to yield 6.43 percent.

Dealers said a stream of heavyweight U.S. economic numbers will dominate the week ahead as markets return from a sleepy holiday period while a number of European centres will also feature, with German statistics in the lead.
The November report on U.S. non-farm payrolls, often seen as the most crucial set of data each month, is due on Friday.

Before that, the U.S. has the National Association of Purchasing Management report and auto sales on Monday, October new home sales on Tuesday, housing completions and the "Beige Book" on economic conditions on Wednesday while jobless claims and non-farm production figures are due out on Thursday.

In Germany, gross domestic product (GDP) for the third quarter is slated for Wednesday while unemployment data is due on Thursday, industrial production from Monday onwards and manufacturing orders from Wednesday.
